status: A (REV A / REV 05): carbon shell 25.4 x 0.5 mm, 6 PEEK radial fins, central Mu-metal conduit 3 mm ID x 0.5 mm wall carrying three twin-axial cables

shielding.coax_external_field: about 0 for an ideal coax (equal and opposite currents): a magnetic conduit adds nothing for coax lines
shielding.note: the conduit matters only for twin-lead; a grounded copper braid / foil already handles the electric coupling

conduit_as_target.note: chi_eff capped at 1000 (demagnetisation, ASSUMED low); the conduit is a soft-ferrous target 30 mm above the coil with a millisecond relaxation

accordion.note: a 6-layer flex cannot fold inside a 25 mm tube; only single-layer flex hinges between rigid panels fold in the space; 0.5 mm boards in 0.5 mm tracks have no fit clearance

shell.note: the 0.1 mm shell alone buckles under the head's moment; the inner layers would have to carry the load (not specified)

heat.note: a 25 mm tube sheds the cable loss by natural convection; the aerogel barrier traps it inside; a closed microfluidic loop with no radiator only moves heat around

metamaterial_core.physical_analogue: 0.1 mm copper sleeve at r 7 mm: transverse cut-off 6.2 kHz, above it the inside field falls like a low effective mu
metamaterial_core.note: no passive kHz-MHz material with mu_r = 0.01 exists outside superconductors; a copper sleeve near the head is itself an eddy target

waveguides.optical: a 10 um core is single-mode (laser + precise coupling); a 1 mm plastic optical fibre is the practical EMI-immune data link (real option, no datasheet on file)
waveguides.em_waveguide: a metal tube of about 5 mm passes nothing below about 35 GHz: no role at PI frequencies

findings: A cables: three RG316-DS (2.9 mm) in a 3 mm conduit fill 280 %: they do not fit (max 1.39 mm each; three RG316-DS need a 6.25 mm bore); mesh overlap {'cable_cable': 2978.0, 'cable_conduit_wall': 1416.5}
A structure: 416 g/m (Garrett two-piece 155 g/m); 1 m tip sag 23.44 mm under a 931 g head; bending 38.2 MPa vs buckling 1191 MPa
A conduit: static shielding x7144, but coax has no external field to shield; as a ferrous target 30 mm above the coil it reads about 1,935 x a 1 g gold at 150 mm, relaxing over 2.65 ms
A accordion: a 6-layer flex needs a 21.6 mm bend radius and a 2-layer hinge 3.6 mm; about 1.9 mm is available: only single-layer hinges (0.9 mm) fold

B shell: 0.1 mm at 30 GPa: bending 182 MPa vs local buckling 143 MPa -> buckles; the cable loss is 11.67 W/m (18.3 K rise in still air, 25.1 K inside the aerogel): convection handles it without a liquid loop; the aerogel makes it worse
B 'metamaterial' and the EM waveguide have no physical role at PI frequencies; the optical data link is the one real idea (a 1 mm POF)
